set_aside.subject: R0-36 replay after ordinary changes
set_aside.text: This holds while the record the first create made keeps its values
set_aside.question: Which later changes mean that a created record no longer “keeps its values,” and what must a retry do after such a change but before erasure or anonymisation?
options: Only erasure or anonymisation ends replay recognition; corrections, archival, restrictions and relationship-state changes do not.
Any change to a value supplied at creation ends replay recognition and the retry is a new create.
A changed record is still recognised, but the retry is refused or returns its current state.
set_aside.default_guess: Only the expressly named erasure or anonymisation ends replay recognition; other changes still identify the original create and return its current record.

witness.initial: The owner creates a customer; Registry commits it, but the answer is lost.
events: The owner corrects that customer's name.
The owner repeats the original record-customer request with the same replay identity.
outcomes: Registry recognises the retry and returns the corrected existing Customer.
Registry treats the changed Customer as no longer covered and creates a second Customer.
witness.observer: The owner sees one customer versus two.

set_aside.subject: R0-36 caller-supplied project id after anonymisation
set_aside.text: Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything that would tell a repeat (R0-06, R0-62); a create repeated after that is a new create, and its answer shows the new record it made.
set_aside.question: What happens when the repeated project create supplied an id that the anonymised project still keeps?
options: The id is reused for a new active project despite R0-62, R0-71 and the existing anonymised record.
Registry mints a different id, despite this being a repeat of a caller-supplied-id create.
The retry is refused because the supplied id remains occupied, despite the new sentence requiring a new record and answer.
set_aside.default_guess: Refuse the retry because an anonymised project retains the supplied id and cannot be replaced or deleted.

witness.initial: In an instance where caller-supplied project ids are allowed, project P is created with id X and the create answer is lost.
events: The owner anonymises P; under R0-62 and R0-87 it retains id X, and under R0-71 this state is final.
The caller repeats the original create with id X.
outcomes: The changed R0-36 makes a new project and returns it.
R0-62, R0-71 and R0-87 leave an existing final anonymised record at X, so the same-id create cannot make that new project and is refused.
witness.observer: The caller sees a successful new project versus a refusal.

set_aside.subject: R0-36 replay after whole-project deletion
set_aside.text: Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything that would tell a repeat
set_aside.question: Does deleting an archived project whole also remove create-replay recognition and make a repeated project create a new create?
options: Yes; both forms of project erasure remove replay recognition.
No; only anonymisation has the newly stated effect, while whole deletion retains replay recognition elsewhere.
The retry is refused or otherwise handled differently after whole deletion.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat whole deletion like anonymisation and make the retry a new create, because the original project record no longer exists.

witness.initial: The owner creates project P; Registry commits it, but the answer is lost.
events: The owner chooses the R0-60 whole-deletion form of project erasure.
The original create request is repeated.
outcomes: Registry has forgotten the create and makes a new project.
Registry retains replay recognition outside the deleted record and returns or refuses based on the former create.
witness.observer: The owner sees a newly created project versus no new project.

set_aside.subject: R0-36 room-create retry after project anonymisation
set_aside.text: a create repeated after that is a new create
set_aside.question: Does “a create” mean only the create corresponding to the erased customer or anonymised project, or every lost-answer create whose record was removed as a consequence, including a room create?
options: Only the matching customer-create or project-create becomes new.
Every affected create, including creation of a room removed by project anonymisation, becomes new.
Room retries follow the add-room preconditions and are refused because the project is archived or erased.
set_aside.default_guess: Scope the exception to the matching customer-create or project-create; a room retry remains subject to add-room preconditions and is refused.

witness.initial: An active project has a newly added room, but the add-room answer is lost.
events: The owner archives and anonymises the project, removing its rooms.
Cabinet Kernel or the owner repeats the original add-room request.
outcomes: The new R0-36 sentence treats the repeated room create as new and returns a new room.
The add-room contract refuses it because the project is archived/anonymised and cannot hold rooms.
witness.observer: The retrying caller sees a room versus a refusal.
